Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-09
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 28 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood - Talent Partner), Liam O'Connor (Redwood - Hiring Manager), Marcus Ng (Candidate)

Summary: Quick screening call for SWE (inference/runtime) role. Walkthrough of Marcus's background in model serving and infra, discussion of team expectations, high level compensation band and interview loop. Agreement to proceed to technical loop; recruiter to coordinate.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey Marcus, uh, thanks for taking the time. You hear me okay?
[00:04] Marcus: Yep I can hear you, thanks for having me.
[00:06] Sophie: Awesome. This is Sophie, I'm the talent partner. Liam, the hiring manager, is here as well. Quick 20-30 minute screen to go over your background, plus logistics. Uh, feel free to be candid about interest and timeline.
[00:18] Liam: Hi Marcus, uh nice to meet you. I run the inference team, just curious about your recent work on serving models at scale.
[00:24] Marcus: Nice to meet you both. Most recently I was at Nimbus Labs where I was on the serving infra team, building a low-latency transformer serving platform, mostly for ranking and search. Worked on batching, KV cache stuff, some quantization experiments and also deployment on k8s with custom autoscalers.
[00:43] Sophie: Nice. Can you give a quick dif \u2014 like, a concise highlight of a project you led?
[00:47] Marcus: Sure. One project I owned was migrating an RPC-based BERT serving stack to a GPU-backed microservice that used continuous batching. Before migration tail latency was around 180 ms p95, after tuning batching and enabling a small KV prefix cache we got p95 down to ~90 ms and throughput up 2.5x. I also worked on a quantized INT8 path which saved ~40% on cost but introduced a small accuracy drop, so we added a quality monitor.
[01:12] Liam: Nice, was the KV cache our usual prefix caching or more of a session cache?
[01:16] Marcus: More prefix cache, so we stored recent key-value states for typical prefix patterns for our ranking queries. It was a custom LRU with TTL; we saw big wins for repeated queries.
[01:23] Sophie: Cool. What about infra tech \u2014 you mentioned k8s and autoscalers, any experience with dedicated GPU pools or multi-tenant scheduling?
[01:30] Marcus: Yeah I worked with node pools and taints, we had a reserved GPU node pool for high-SLA tenants and burstable pools for others. I implemented a scheduler hook that would prefer hot KV cache nodes for affinity to reduce cold-cache hits.
[01:42] Liam: That sounds aligned. For this role we care a lot about latency-sensitive workloads and graceful degradation \u2014 can you talk about fallback strategies you've used?
[01:50] Marcus: Sure. We used model-variant fallbacks; if a heavy model path saturated, we'd route to a quantized faster variant or an earlier cached response. We also had region-based fallback and a degraded-response mode that returned compact summaries instead of full answers under load.
[02:06] Sophie: On the people side, are you interviewing elsewhere or have a timeline?
[02:10] Marcus: I'm talking to a couple places \u2014 mostly infra-focused teams. I'm hoping to make a decision in the next 3-4 weeks. I have about a 3 week notice period but could do some overlap.
[02:19] Sophie: Good to know. Any constraints on location or work authorization?
[02:22] Marcus: I'm currently in Toronto, remote-first OK, open to occasional travel. I have full work authorization in Canada and currently on a US visa that requires sponsorship \u2014 I can share details off-line.
[02:33] Liam: From a skills match, can you dive a bit deeper into kernel/op-level optimizations you worked on?
[02:37] Marcus: Sure \u2014 I did some profiling on aten/cuda ops and optimized matmul calls by reorganizing attention inputs to increase memory coalescing. Also tuned cudnn paths and experimented with grouped attention kernels \u2014 small wins but compounding. Some of that required compiler flags and careful tensor memory layouts.
[02:53] Sophie: That's great. How comfortable are you with Python + C++ hybrid stacks and deploying compiled kernels?
[02:58] Marcus: Very comfortable. Our stack used Python for orchestration, but performance-critical kernels were in C++/CUDA. I wrote bindings and CI to test numerical parity after optimizations.
[03:08] Liam: Do you have experience with model compilation toolchains \u2014 Triton, TVM, or custom compilers?
[03:13] Marcus: We used a mix: experimented with Triton for a couple ops, and used XLA for certain workloads. TVM was used in a research pipeline but not heavily in production.
[03:21] Liam: Any experience with quantization-aware training or post-training quantization?
[03:25] Marcus: Both. For some ranking models we did post-training dynamic quant and for a couple small models we did QAT to recover accuracy.
[03:31] Sophie: Cool. On compensation, are you looking for anything specific? Very high-level just so we can align.
[03:36] Marcus: Ideally in the mid-senior band \u2014 I'm targeting around the 140k-170k USD base equivalent range, open to equity/bonus.
[03:44] Sophie: Sounds reasonable. For Redwood the typical band for this level is in that neighborhood; we'll share the specific band when we proceed.
[03:51] Liam: Marcus, do you have any public code or a portfolio we can review quickly?
[03:55] Marcus: Yeah I can send links \u2014 most of my repos are infra helpers and a toy transformer serving benchmark. I'll send two links after this call.
[04:03] Sophie: Great. The interview loop would be a technical screen + system design + take-home or pair-prog depending on the team; expect 3-4 interviews, about 2-3 hours total. Does that work for you?
[04:15] Marcus: Yep. That works.
[04:16] Liam: Any red flags we should know about?
[04:18] Marcus: Nothing particular, I left my last role for more ownership on infra and better impact on product latency, not for comp reasons.
[04:25] Sophie: Cool. One operational question: are you okay with occasional on-call rotations?
[04:29] Marcus: Yes, I've done paging with escalation, I'm used to 1:8 pager rotation.
[04:34] Liam: One more skill question \u2014 experience with observability and instrumentation?
[04:37] Marcus: Prometheus, Grafana, and custom tracing. We hooked p95 metrics to autoscaler thresholds and built regression alerts tied to canary datasets. Also used synthetic benchmarks for perf regressions.
[04:48] Sophie: Nice. Any questions for us about team culture or process?
[04:52] Marcus: Just curious about the balance of infra vs product \u2014 is this role more platform-infra or embedded with application teams?
[04:58] Liam: It's mainly platform-facing but with close partnership to product teams \u2014 you'll own the runtime and also define SLAs with consumers. We expect 60/40 infra to product.
[05:08] Marcus: That sounds like my preference.
[05:10] Sophie: Logistics \u2014 next step is the technical loop. I'm going to send a calendar invite with some slots; can you share availability for next week?
[05:17] Marcus: I can do Tues/Wed afternoons PST or Thurs morning.
[05:20] Sophie: Perfect. We'll try to accommodate. Anything else we should capture?
[05:23] Liam: Maybe a quick note on tooling: do you have strong Rust experience? We use Rust in some low-level components.
[05:30] Marcus: I've written small Rust services, not daily driver but comfortable reading and contributing.
[05:34] Sophie: Okay great. We'll proceed. Marcus, thanks again. We'll follow up with the loop details.
[05:40] Marcus: Thank you both. Looking forward to it.
[05:42] [end of recorded transcript]

Notes: A few transcription artifacts: "KV cache" transcribed consistently, occasional filler tokens. Candidate seems to have direct experience aligned to role. Recruiter to handle scheduling and compensation alignment.
